summary: Owner directive (2026-11-28), recorded as a study-queue entry per CONTINUOUS_LEARNING_AND_GROWTH.md: Michelle Rogers is to keep studying MORE of the categories of business, beyond the current catalogue's centre of gravity. CURRENT STATE: the open-courseware catalogue already in the knowledge base holds 29 free courses from 9 university providers across 8 areas — computer-science fundamentals, software engineering and web development, AI/ML, data science and statistics, cloud/DevOps, cybersecurity, entrepreneurship and fundraising, and mathematics for computer science. QUEUE ORDER SET BY THIS DIRECTIVE: business-facing study first — the entrepreneurship and fundraising courses already in the catalogue are worked before the technical areas, then data science applied to business decisions (pricing, funder reporting, platform metrics); the technical areas continue after, they are not dropped. NEXT RESEARCH TASK (queued, not started): extend the catalogue with free, non-expiring courses in five additional business categories — business finance and accounting, marketing, operations management, business law basics, and sales and partnership development — following the same standards as the original sweep: free with no expiring trial, a reputable provider (university or equivalent), and every course entered with its subject, provider, and free-terms provenance so a later reader can check the claim. Each completed course then produces its own filed lesson under the learning loop, naming the duty it improves. STATUS: queued at the owner's direction on 2026-11-28; no new courses have been researched or entered yet, and nothing in this entry should be read as a completed expansion. APPLICATION: improves CONTINUOUS_LEARNING_AND_GROWTH.md (curriculum priorities, section 1) and, as the business courses are completed, the grant playbook and correspondence practice they feed. Filed unverified by design: an internal directive and queue record, not a checked external source.
title: Business study expansion — owner directive (2026-11-28) to study more categories of business; queue order and next research task
